heading: You already paid for the room's attention. It's leaking out anyway.
subhead: Between the meeting that ran long, the second screen nobody can hear, and the Tuesday quiz night nobody knew was on — venues lose guests to friction, not to a lack of things worth staying for.

cards.title: The show's on. Nobody in the bar knows.
cards.text: Dinner & a show, poolside sets and function rooms live on different signs — front desk becomes the wayfinding desk, and guests never discover the dining room, the late bar, or what's on in your auditorium.

cards.title: One speaker system, four kick-offs
cards.text: Only one match gets the house sound. Silent commentary reads as low energy, and fans of the "other" game leave for somewhere where they can connect.

cards.title: Nobody knew it was on
cards.text: Trivia, music and comedy live and die on a poster. Locals need a reason to check, not just a reason to come — and marketing gets scattered across three apps you don't own.
